elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle (definitions table); ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate', claimed by its id and never expanded. 'Driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle') is no aggregate: ru.aggregate is 'Not a stand-in for ... a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle', so the role is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency). Mapping index: 'The driver of a vehicle' maps to the same aggregate.

The entry onto or across the highway is where the subject's footprint comes onto its roadway: rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (roadway, ...)'; st.roadway 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder'; st.on_way 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on' ties that roadway to the highway; st.highway 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders' carries DEF-NRS-484A-095 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority'. st.highway's exclusion ('Not a stand-in for: the roadway') is respected: the roadway is its own atom, the highway only anchors it. kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' tells a moving entry from a vehicle standing at the edge. 'About to' is an imminent movement, read by the movement itself (ontology, what is not an atom).

DEF-NRS-484A-190: a private way is 'every way or place in private ownership and used for vehicular travel by the owner'. st.driveway_or_alley_entrance is a 'private road, alley or driveway meeting the highway'; its exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: which of them meets the highway there' is why the rule adds st.alley ('a narrow way within a block serving the rear of properties'): an alley is a highway (DEF-NRS-484A-015 'Alley means a highway'), not a private way, so the subject must overlap the entrance and no alley region. rel.occupies anchors both to the subject's footprint.

Mapping index: 'shall yield' maps to kin.speed, rel.contact. The yield is judged while the subject moves (kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' above the halt tolerance): a subject at rest grants precedence. rel.contact 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)' is a failure to yield; its exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: a near miss' is respected, since the near conflict is the operationalization of s5.

'vehicles' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle. 'on such highway' singles out the highway the subject enters: the other vehicle's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a travel region (st.travel_region, 'the union of the kinds a device can govern: a lane ..., a roadway ..., a shoulder, or an intersection') lying (st.on_way) on that same highway region, re-bound with the selection of s2. st.travel_region's exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: the extent of a highway' is respected: the highway is read through st.on_way, the travel region only locates the vehicle. 'approaching': the vehicle moves (kin.speed above the halt tolerance) and the subject lies ahead of it, rel.bearing 'direction of b from a in a's frame' with a positive longitudinal component.

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: DEF-NRS-484A-210 'approaching under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash unless one grants precedence to the other'
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: under constant velocities (direction and speed of both), the two centres reach their closest approach within the time-to-collision threshold at a centre distance below the collision clearance; such a pair is in danger of a crash unless the subject grants precedence

applicability: The subject (vehicle aggregate) is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) and its footprint overlaps both a roadway region r lying on a highway region h and a driveway_or_alley_entrance region e, and overlaps no alley region; its overlap with e has held at every observation since one at which it overlapped e and did not overlap r (the subject came onto the entrance from off the roadway: formula 'since').
obligation: For every selection of h, r and e satisfying the applicability's conditions at this observation (re-bound in full): for every other road user v of the vehicle aggregate that is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance), whose footprint overlaps a travel region lying on h, and in whose frame the subject lies ahead (longitudinal component of rel.bearing from v to the subject positive): the subject and v are not in contact (rel.contact), and it is not the case that their closest approach falls within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance).

narrowings.why: 'driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it

'about to enter or cross' is an imminent movement, read by the entering movement itself: the rule judges every observation at which the moving subject straddles the private way's entrance and a roadway of the highway, having come onto the entrance from off the roadway; the rest of a crossing is judged through the closest approach under constant velocities that each such observation predicts

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject vehicle rolls out of a driveway entrance region onto roadway r of highway h, kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance, overlapping no alley. Vehicle v moves in a lane on h with the subject ahead of it (rel.bearing longitudinal positive); prim.closest_approach_within holds over p.conflict_horizon and prim.closest_approach_distance is below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but v is far up the lane: their closest approach does not fall within p.conflict_horizon, and no contact occurs.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject drives along roadway r of h and its footprint never overlaps a driveway_or_alley_entrance region; v approaches from behind.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but st.on_way is not observed on the source: which highway the roadway r and v's lane lie on is unknown, so whether the subject is entering such a highway and whether v approaches on that same highway are unknown, while the subject straddles the entrance and the roadway and the closest approach is a conflict.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject rolls out of a driveway entrance onto roadway r of h and no other road user is in the scene: the duty binds the subject alone and is met.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The subject comes out of an alley: its footprint overlaps an st.alley region and the entrance region as it reaches roadway r, with v in conflict as in forbid. An alley is a highway, not a private way.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition standard's vehicle-state estimates

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: traffic-conflict technique literature (Hyden; FHWA Surrogate Safety Assessment Model)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
